title: Sub-Scope Package Preparation Delivery
summary: add collection-local checkbox selection and extend Prepare Package to exact sub-scope documents as an explicitly export-only workflow
content_html:
Sub-Scope Package Preparation Delivery

Status And Order

In progress as SSI-3, after Sub-Scope Detail Delete Delivery. SSI-3.0 froze the selection, collection, package, provenance, and export-only boundaries below. SSI-3.1 extracted the shared immutable selection rules and added the independent sub-scope owner without changing the visible Index. SSI-3.2 added the manage-only collection controls. SSI-3.3 now extends the existing package path through exact configured child sources and keeps every child run export-only. Delivery is at the SSI-3.3 review gate before the final SSI-3.4 acceptance and closeout slice.

SSI-3 is the broadest delivery. It follows SSI-2 so the manage controller, capability projection, busy/error handling, collection refresh, public isolation, and realistic header/list layout have already been proved by a smaller exact-target workflow.

Complete Outcome

Manage mode gives a docs_subscope list the same compact selection language as the main Index:

  • an Actions control enters selection mode;
  • checkboxes appear as siblings to row navigation;
  • Select all, Clear, and Done control the current collection selection; and
  • the sub-scope Actions menu offers Prepare package… for one or more checked documents.

The package workflow reads exact sources from { scope, sub_scope }, validates checked IDs against that collection, and records the complete collection identity in package provenance.

Every package prepared from a sub-scope is export-only in this delivery. It is not actionable in Returned Packages, Docs Review, or Docs Import.

This completes outbound preparation of the seeded tag documents, not an automated round trip. Sub-Scope Returned Package Review Delivery separately allows a complete returned package to stop at immutable Docs Review; SSI-3 does not imply that enriched package records can be applied back to the child sources.

Change Classification

kind work
shipped and retained compact Index Actions/selection interaction; pure selection transitions; Prepare Package modal; package profiles and engine
refactored isolate collection-neutral selection transitions and package source-context mechanics while preserving current Index behavior
extended add a separate sub-scope selection owner and optional sub_scope package request/source/provenance support
genuinely new sub-scope checkboxes, list Actions/selection controls, and package preparation from checked child documents

The same interaction system is reused; the Index and sub-scope collection keep separate state owners and cannot supply targets to one another.

Selection Contract

The sub-scope selection owner is keyed by { scope, sub_scope }.

  • Only checked IDs are action targets.
  • Opening Actions enters selection mode but does not preselect the parent report or an unvalidated detail target.
  • Checkbox clicks do not navigate.
  • Shift-check extends from the collection's range anchor across currently visible eligible rows.
  • Row navigation remains available while selection is active.
  • Returning from detail to the same mounted collection may preserve selection.
  • Inventory refresh prunes missing IDs and retains eligible checked IDs.
  • Collection change, report unmount, leaving manage mode, or Done clears the owner according to the accepted lifecycle.
  • Select all replaces checked IDs with the currently visible eligible rows supplied by the collection projection. Before SSI-4 filtering, every eligible collection row is visible, so this remains whole-collection selection.
  • Clear empties checked IDs.
  • Done exits and clears selection.
  • The compact command group does not add a selected-count label.

The sub-scope action menu contains only capabilities deliberately adopted by this feature. Copy, Move, bulk Delete, scope actions, and Review Package do not appear merely because the main Index menu supports them.

Package Contract

The existing Prepare Package workflow remains the modal and export owner. A sub-scope request adds one normalized collection field:

scope:     <parent scope>
sub_scope: <configured child>
doc_ids:   <effective checked IDs>

The browser and service must:

  • list and validate documents from the configured child source root;
  • treat the collection as flat and never infer parent-scope descendants;
  • derive effective IDs after supported visibility/summary options;
  • never add an ID excluded by the submitted checked selection;
  • resolve selection and source records by doc_id, never title;
  • render content through the existing package engine;
  • include scope, sub_scope, selected/exported IDs, profile, and generated time in internal provenance and result payloads;
  • project sub-scope runs as supports_return_import: false, even when the same profile supports return for a top-level scope;
  • omit or replace return/import instructions in external context for that export-only projection; and
  • exclude the resulting metadata/files from actionable returned-package listing and review.

Top-level scope package preparation remains unchanged when sub_scope is absent.

In Scope

  • One sub-scope Actions control and menu containing Prepare Package only.
  • Collection-local checkbox gutters and Select all/Clear/Done.
  • Reuse or extraction of pure selection transitions without changing main Index behavior.
  • A separate collection-keyed selection owner and lifecycle.
  • Optional sub_scope support across the package browser client, config, documents, context, prepare request, source loader, engine handoff, result, activity, and metadata.
  • Flat-collection effective-selection rules.
  • Explicit export-only projection and returned-review exclusion.
  • Non-viewable, missing-summary, stale-ID, empty-selection, cancel, success, failure, and retry evidence.
  • Public/manage module isolation and narrow/dense UI review.

Not In Scope

  • Returned-package review, Docs Review materialization, or Docs Import from a sub-scope package.
  • Copy, Move, bulk Delete, or any other selection action.
  • Parent/descendant expansion inside a flat sub-scope.
  • Selecting the parent report or documents from another collection.
  • Package profile redesign, new external service adapters, or a new package engine.
  • Tag Registry reads, group-based filtering, deduplication, or synchronization.
  • General report filtering/search or main Index interaction redesign.

Frozen SSI-3.0 Contract

Selection Ownership

The current docs-viewer-index-selection.js combines two different concerns. SSI-3.1 may extract only these collection-neutral immutable transitions:

  • normalize and deduplicate IDs while retaining input order;
  • enter, toggle, Shift-range, Select all, Clear, Done, and reconcile; and
  • replace selection with caller-supplied visible eligible IDs.

The main Index retains its own scope/view lifecycle owner, DOM gutter and projection helpers, active displayed-document preselection, and documentIndex eligibility. Existing Index control IDs, action resolution, range behavior, reload reconciliation, and package invocation remain unchanged.

The sub-scope contribution adds a separate owner keyed by normalized { scope, sub_scope }. It receives collection membership only from the shared report's explicit documents and lifecycle events. It:

  • enters empty when the collection Actions control opens;
  • never preselects the parent report, displayed child, URL subdoc, focused row, or main Index selection;
  • uses the report's ordered visible eligible IDs for range and Select all;
  • preserves checked IDs while list/detail state changes within the same mounted collection;
  • prunes missing IDs on an explicit report refresh; and
  • exits and clears on Done, report unmount, collection-key change, or leaving manage mode.

docs-viewer-action-definitions.js and its SELECTION / ALL resolver are already collection-neutral and remain the sole Prepare Package target resolver. The main Index and sub-scope controllers supply their own checked IDs to separate resolver contexts.

Collection And Request Boundary

The normalized collection identity is:

top-level: { scope }
child:     { scope, sub_scope }

An absent sub_scope preserves every current top-level request and response. When present, sub_scope must be a non-blank configured one-level child of the submitted parent scope. Unknown children, extra collection fields, path-like IDs, and implicit fallback to the parent source reject.

The browser extends the existing endpoints rather than adding parallel package routes:

GET  /docs/packages/config?scope=<scope>&sub_scope=<sub_scope>
GET  /docs/packages/documents?scope=<scope>&sub_scope=<sub_scope>
POST /docs/packages/prepare
     { scope, sub_scope, profile_id, doc_ids, select_all: false,
       missing_summary_only, include_non_viewable, target_format,
       content_format, dry_run, activity_context }

For the child branch, select_all: true rejects. doc_ids must be the non-empty effective checked selection calculated by the modal. The service revalidates every ID against the exact configured child source; an ID found only in the parent scope or another sub-scope is unknown.

The config response validates the requested child and projects every enabled profile as supports_return_import: false for that request without modifying the stored profile. The documents response repeats scope and sub_scope, identifies a flat sub-scope selection model, and returns source-derived title, summary, viewability, and content-length records required by the existing modal. The compact report inventory is not a package source because it does not contain that data.

Flat Effective Selection

The package source loader reuses configured collection resolution, then loads and validates Markdown directly under the child document root. It does not load parent-scope documents or infer hierarchy from parent IDs.

  • The descendants control is absent for a sub-scope package.
  • Profile descendant defaults or tree requirements never add child IDs.
  • Missing-summary and non-viewable choices may only subtract from submitted checked IDs.
  • Profile limits may truncate that already confined sequence.
  • The service orders resolved records by the child source projection and rejects any submitted stale or cross-collection ID.
  • selected = exported + failed + skipped remains the auditable package accounting rule.

The document-content profile remains the intended tag-document enrichment profile. document-tree may project the exact checked flat records as roots, but it gains no descendant semantics.

Result, Provenance, Activity, And Context

A successful or failed child prepare result repeats:

scope
sub_scope
profile_id
supports_return_import: false
selected_doc_ids
exported_doc_ids
counts and issues

Internal metadata records mandatory scope, sub_scope, and supports_return_import: false beside the existing export identity and checked IDs. External context records the same collection identity and export-only flag, and includes a non-editable notice that returned-package review/import is unsupported. Existing editable profile context remains profile-owned; SSI-3 does not introduce per-sub-scope context persistence or mutate the stored profile merely to create an export-only projection.

The management event and Studio Activity entry retain the parent scope, sub_scope, profile, export ID, and effective document IDs. They do not label the package as a top-level scope package or an importable result.

Return And Public Boundary

The run-scoped export-only projection is service-enforced even when the stored profile normally supports return import. A staged child package:

  • cannot enter the actionable returned-package files collection;
  • is reported as blocked with an export-only sub-scope reason;
  • is rejected by direct Review Package and Docs Import entrypoints before source materialization or writes; and
  • cannot become importable by removing sub_scope from a browser request, because trusted internal metadata remains authoritative.

Public routes retain the shared read-only report, load no selection/package management module, and expose no package endpoints or controls.

Test-Owned Fixture Matrix

case fixture expectation
ordinary flat collection two checked synthetic child documents export exactly once in child source order
visible eligibility Select all receives the report's explicit visible eligible IDs and replaces, rather than extends, the checked set
non-viewable inclusion choice may retain or subtract the checked child but never add another record
missing summary filter may subtract a checked child with a summary and keeps exact accounting
stale or missing ID an ID absent from the exact child rejects without package output
cross-collection parent-only and sibling-sub-scope-only IDs reject even when valid elsewhere
no descendants parent-like front matter and the tree profile do not expand beyond checked child IDs
owner isolation Index and two different sub-scope collection owners cannot exchange checked IDs or anchors
cancel/failure/retry cancellation writes nothing; failure retains selection and a retry uses the same exact collection
returned package trusted child metadata remains blocked and direct review/import writes nothing
public isolation public report renders without importing management selection or package modules

All write and route evidence uses temporary configured sources and an isolated writable projects base. The real Analysis tags collection is a later manual read/review surface; SSI-3 tests do not package or mutate its documents.

Delivery Tracker

[x] SSI-3.0 — Freeze Selection And Package Boundaries

  • [x] Trace current Index selection transitions, owner lifecycle, gutter, Actions controls, resolver, lazy workflow, and package service/profile owners.
  • [x] Record which logic is collection-neutral and which remains Index-specific.
  • [x] Define visible eligible IDs as the explicit Select all input without changing the unfiltered main Index result.
  • [x] Define exact optional-sub_scope request, response, metadata, activity, and export-only projection contracts.
  • [x] Add test-owned flat, non-viewable, missing-summary, missing-ID, and cross-collection fixtures.
  • [x] Capture green top-level Index selection and package baselines.

Review gate passed: the separation between shared pure rules, the two state owners, and the package collection boundary was accepted before runtime edits.

SSI-3.0 Evidence

  • The pure immutable transitions and Select all input are currently colocated with the Index-specific lifecycle owner and DOM helpers in docs-viewer-index-selection.js; only the transitions are candidates for extraction.
  • The existing action registry already resolves Prepare Package from checked SELECTION with ALL. The Index controller separately owns active-document preselection, view lifecycle, descendant-aware modal input, lazy workflow loading, and checked-ID handoff.
  • The package client currently has top-level-only config/documents requests. The workflow and request model carry scope plus exact doc_ids; the service and export source context currently load only a top-level scope. Metadata and returned-package validation already enforce supports_return_import, giving SSI-3 one authoritative export-only gate to extend.
  • The shared report already supplies explicit collection identity, ordered documents, row-leading and list-toolbar hosts, and mount/state/refresh/unmount events. No report or URL scraping is required.
  • Existing top-level browser baselines passed: docs_viewer_index_selection_modules.py, docs_viewer_prepare_package_workflow_modules.py, and the real manage-route docs_viewer_prepare_package_workflow_route.py.
  • Focused top-level package service and export tests passed 47 passed, 1 skipped using an isolated writable projects base. The first collection attempt used .env.local and failed before tests ran because its external workspace was not writable in the sandbox; the isolated rerun is the product baseline.
  • No runtime, profile, package output, generated payload, or Analysis tag-document source changed in SSI-3.0.

[x] SSI-3.1 — Reuse Selection Rules Without Index Drift

  • [x] Extract or parameterize only the pure selection transitions needed by both owners.
  • [x] Make Select all replace the checked set with explicit visible eligible IDs supplied by the owning collection.
  • [x] Keep current Index Actions, checkboxes, range behavior, lifecycle, selected targets, and package behavior unchanged.
  • [x] Add a sub-scope owner keyed by { scope, sub_scope }.
  • [x] Prove state cannot cross between Index and sub-scope collections.

SSI-3.1 Evidence

  • docs-viewer-selection-rules.js now owns only immutable ID normalization, enter, toggle, Shift-range, Select all replacement, Clear, exit, and reconciliation. docs-viewer-index-selection.js retains its existing public names plus the Index-specific owner, scope/view lifecycle, gutter, and DOM projection.
  • docs-viewer-subscope-selection.js adds one owner keyed by normalized { scope, sub_scope }. It accepts the shared report's existing mount/state/refresh/unmount event shapes, enters empty, preserves state across same-collection list/detail events, prunes on refresh, and clears on collection change, manage exit, Done, or unmount.
  • docs_viewer_index_selection_modules.py --site-root .: passed. Its synthetic owner matrix covered immutable state, ordered deduplication, explicit Select all replacement, Shift-range, refresh pruning, normalized collection identity, unavailable entry, two child owners, Index/child action target isolation, collection change, manage exit, and unmount.
  • Existing parity checks passed: docs_viewer_index_selection_lifecycle_route.py, docs_viewer_prepare_package_workflow_modules.py --site-root ., and docs_viewer_prepare_package_workflow_route.py. These retain the real manage-route Index lifecycle and current top-level Prepare Package flow.
  • Maintained explicit lint passed for the three changed JavaScript runtime files and the one changed Python smoke. git diff --check passed.
  • No sub-scope report contribution, visible control, package request/service, profile, package output, returned-package workflow, or Analysis tag document changed in SSI-3.1.

Review gate passed: the focused Index-parity and independent sub-scope-owner evidence was accepted before SSI-3.2 added visible collection controls.

[x] SSI-3.2 — Add Collection Selection UI

  • [x] Contribute the list Actions control, Prepare Package item, checkbox gutters, and Select all/Clear/Done group.
  • [x] Keep row navigation and checkbox activation separate and retain Shift-range selection across visible eligible rows.
  • [x] Reconcile list/detail navigation, Back/Forward, inventory refresh, unmount, and manage/public changes.
  • [x] Preserve Status/non-viewable icons and exact row IDs.
  • [x] Review realistic dense and narrow Analysis tags layouts.

SSI-3.2 Evidence

  • The manage-only report contribution now owns one collection Actions control, a Prepare Package item, row-leading checkboxes, and the compact Select all, Clear, and Done group. It consumes the independent sub-scope owner and the shared report's explicit collection, document, and lifecycle inputs.
  • Checkbox activation stops before row navigation. Shift-range and Select all receive only the report's ordered current IDs. Same-mount list/detail return preserves checked IDs; refresh reconciliation, collection change, manage exit, Done, and unmount retain the accepted clearing/pruning rules.
  • Prepare Package resolves exact checked IDs through the shared action registry. The visible item intentionally remains disabled with Sub-scope package preparation is unavailable. because SSI-3.3 has not adopted the package client, modal, or service.
  • docs_viewer_subscope_report_modules.py --site-root .: passed. Synthetic coverage proved empty entry, exact row IDs, separate checkbox/navigation activation, ordered three-row Shift-range, exact future { scope, sub_scope, doc_ids } handoff, Select all, Clear, Done, Escape, outside-click, list/detail retention, status/non-viewable icons, Delete contribution coexistence, and public module isolation.
  • docs_viewer_index_selection_modules.py --site-root ., docs_viewer_service_manage.py --timeout-ms 20000, and public_docs_viewer_readonly.py --site-root site: passed using isolated localhost servers and a temporary writable projects base where required.
  • Real Analysis tags review inspected all 248 projected rows at 1280 × 720. Opening Actions entered empty selection; Shift-checking absence through ambiguity retained those three exact IDs without navigation or package output. List/detail return retained them, browser Back restored the detail target, browser Forward remounted the list and cleared the owner, and Done exited with zero checked IDs.
  • At 390 × 844 the 354-pixel report, Actions menu, compact commands, checkbox gutter, and rows stayed inside the report with no report-child overflow. The existing global manage top bar still projects a 512-pixel row and is not changed or claimed by SSI-3.2. Browser diagnostics reported no log entries.
  • Maintained explicit JavaScript/Python lint and git diff --check passed. No package request/service, profile, export, returned-package workflow, public control, generated package output, or Analysis tag-document source changed.

Review gate passed: the list interaction was accepted before SSI-3.3 began package service adoption.

[x] SSI-3.3 — Extend Package Preparation

  • [x] Extend package reads and requests with optional configured sub_scope.
  • [x] Resolve source and effective IDs within that exact child collection.
  • [x] Keep top-level profile and package behavior unchanged.
  • [x] Record complete collection identity in result, activity, internal metadata, and external provenance where applicable.
  • [x] Force sub-scope preparation into an honest export-only projection.
  • [x] Exclude sub-scope package output from returned review/import workflows.
  • [x] Prove submitted IDs and exported records agree exactly.

SSI-3.3 Evidence

  • The existing config, documents, and prepare endpoints now accept one optional configured sub_scope. Child config and documents repeat the exact collection identity, mark the source flat, and project every enabled profile as export-only without mutating stored profile data. Blank, unknown, path-like, alias-field, select_all: true, parent-only, sibling-child-only, and stale targets fail closed.
  • The package loader resolves the configured child root and validates Markdown there directly. Missing-summary, non-viewable, and profile-limit rules only subtract from submitted checked IDs. The tree profile emits exact checked child records as roots and never expands parent-like front matter.
  • Child results, management events, Studio Activity, internal metadata, and external context retain scope, sub_scope, profile, effective selected and exported IDs, and supports_return_import: false. External context includes the non-actionable return/import notice.
  • A synthetic two-record write produced the exact checked records once in child source order. Trusted child metadata was excluded from actionable Returned Packages and Docs Import listings; direct Review Package and Import rejected before review-source materialization or document writes. The export-only block also applies to the flat tree profile.
  • Focused Python coverage passed 90 passed across package service, export, Activity, returned-package parsing, and Docs Import collection contracts. The service subset passed all 28 tests with its isolated HTTP route fixture enabled.
  • docs_viewer_prepare_package_workflow_modules.py, docs_viewer_subscope_report_modules.py, and the existing real manage-route docs_viewer_prepare_package_workflow_route.py passed. They proved optional child queries, flat modal projection, exact request composition, lazy report bridge wiring, cancel selection retention, public isolation, and unchanged top-level preparation.
  • A fresh isolated local service rendered the real 248-row Analysis tags report. Checking only absence opened a one-document modal with no visible descendants control and both profiles labelled export-only. Cancel retained that exact checked ID, restored focus to Actions, wrote no package, and produced no browser warning/error logs.
  • Explicit maintained JavaScript/Python lint, Python compilation, and git diff --check passed. No real Analysis tag source, stored package profile, persistent package output, or public package capability changed.

Review gate: isolated dry-run/write evidence proves exact package contents, provenance, containment, and non-actionable return status.

[ ] SSI-3.4 — End-To-End Acceptance And Closeout

  • [ ] Run focused selection, controller, package model/client/service/engine, metadata, returned-list exclusion, activity, and public isolation checks.
  • [ ] Run route/browser evidence with synthetic source and an isolated writable projects base.
  • [ ] Manually review ordinary, dense, narrow, cancel, success, unavailable, and retry states without mutating real Analysis documents.
  • [ ] Run the maintained Docs Viewer profile at the integration boundary.
  • [ ] Independently review the final diff and exact output/omission claims.
  • [ ] Transfer only shipped contracts to durable selection, package, report, and Sub-Scope Index owners.

Completion Gate

SSI-3 is complete only when checked IDs from one exact sub-scope produce one auditable export-only package, current Index selection/package behavior remains unchanged, and no return/import or public capability has been implied.
